headline: Light rain this evening and a round of showers Sunday afternoon stay well short of flooding amounts; the Coastal Flood Warning still starts 6 AM Monday ahead of Tuesday's stronger, tropical-moisture storm.

summary.text: RRFS and NBM now put the wettest 3 hours on Sunday afternoon (1 to 4 PM) instead of Saturday night, at 0.20 and 0.12 in. Still small: no flooding burst in sight before Tuesday.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: RRFS 0.20, NBM 0.12, HRRR 0.10, GFS 0.10, ECMWF 0.05 in. Consensus about 0.13 in (0.10 last evening). RRFS is the wettest; all agree it stays light.
No street flooding expected through Monday. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; the wettest single hour in any model is 0.10 in.
Light rain starting around 6 PM tonight, lingering lightly to about midnight. Showers Sunday roughly 1 to 4 PM. Monday dry. Heavier storm Tuesday into Wednesday.
Tides running about 1.0 to 1.4 ft above prediction. Tonight's rain falls on the rising tide toward the 6.6 ft high at 10:19 PM; Sunday's showers fall near low tide. Channel low: 0.18 ft at Alameda.
Nothing needed this weekend. Use dry Monday: clear street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and plan where cars go for Tuesday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A cold, clear start this morning ahead of the next upper trough (NWS San Francisco, 12:59 AM and 3:38 AM). A cold front brings rain late today, with the best chance near SFO between about 9 PM and 1 AM, then northwesterly winds and post-frontal showers into Sunday; NWS Marine expects another round Sunday morning into the afternoon. Monday is a brief break and, per NWS, the best day to prepare. Tuesday's system taps tropical moisture, with moderate to heavy rain Tuesday into Wednesday and strong winds, on top of the king tides and surge; NWS says the storm door stays open into the end of November. Tuesday's storm is still just beyond this snapshot's 72-hour model window, which ends early Tuesday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since last evening's discussion, the coastal flood products are unchanged, and the rain guidance shifted rather than grew. Wettest 3 hours / total in the next 72 hours:
• HRRR (2 AM Sat run): 0.10 / 0.17 in, wettest 3 hours this evening around 5 to 8 PM, with its wettest hour 0.07 in. Its run ends Sunday evening. The 15-minute output shows 0.02 in in the first 15 minutes around 6 PM, then a steady 0.01 in or less per 15 minutes to about midnight.
• RRFS (10 PM Fri run): 0.20 / 0.23 in, all of it Sunday afternoon, wettest 3 hours about 1 to 4 PM with a 0.10 in hour. Last evening it had 0.10 in on Sunday evening; the shower round is now a bit stronger and about 4 hours earlier.
• NBM: 0.12 / 0.15 in, also Sunday 1 to 4 PM (last evening 0.05 in, Saturday night).
• GFS 0.10 / 0.17 in, Saturday evening, matching HRRR hour for hour. ECMWF 0.05 / 0.10 in, spread lightly over Saturday evening and night.

Consensus (HRRR 0.10 × 1.25 = 0.13, RRFS 0.20, NBM 0.12): about 0.13 in, up from 0.10 in. Even with HRRR's history of under-forecasting bursts by about 3×, tonight would stay near 0.30 in in 3 hours, under the 0.71 in Yellow threshold. Sunday's RRFS cell is the kind of convective shower NWS has flagged; it is supported by NBM, so it is a real signal, but its 0.10 in hour is a quarter of the 0.40 in that would matter.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.0 to 1.4 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City, a little less than yesterday's 1.5 ft. This morning's 8.4 ft high at 9:06 AM runs about 9.7 ft. Tonight's rain falls on the rising tide toward the 6.6 ft high at 10:19 PM (about 8.1 ft on the model around 11 PM), so drainage slows late in the evening, but the amounts are small. Sunday's 8.8 ft high at 9:42 AM runs about 10.2 ft, before the showers; the afternoon showers then fall on the falling tide toward the -0.4 ft low at 4:53 PM (about 0.7 ft on the model), good timing for drainage. The model run ends 7 PM Sunday, so Monday's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM and Tuesday's 9.5 ft high at 11:02 AM are not covered yet.

The Coastal Flood Advisory runs until 6 AM Monday, then the Coastal Flood Warning (up to 3 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways) through 4 PM Thursday. NWS expects San Francisco high tides 2.9 ft above normal Tuesday and 3.0 ft Wednesday, including up to 1.8 ft of surge. Tuesday's and Wednesday's late-morning highs are the overlap to watch: high tides with surge slow the channel's drainage.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.18 ft at 4 AM, flat overnight (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). The gauge upstream of Caltrain has not reported since 5:13 PM Friday (0.07 ft then; Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft), so it is about 11 hours stale.

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry overnight. The Caltrain rain gauge has not reported since 5:13 PM Friday (0.12 in over the 24 hours before that), so there is no current local rain reading. The Alameda channel gauge is low and steady.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low for the weekend: all five models keep the wettest 3 hours at 0.20 in or less and no hour above 0.10 in. The main question is how strong Sunday afternoon's showers get, with RRFS and NBM agreeing on timing. Tuesday's storm is the real concern, but it is not yet in this snapshot's models, so its timing, intensity and overlap with the late-morning king tides will come in the next discussions.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars this weekend.
• Monday (dry, before the warning-level tides and Tuesday's rain): clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and decide where cars will go if Tuesday's rain lands near a high tide. Power outages from Tuesday's wind can slow the pumps.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the morning high tides; don't walk or drive through moving water.
